entities.name: Adrien Maurice de Noailles
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Adrien Maurice de Noailles, 3rd Duke of Noailles, was a French Royal Army officer born in 1737 in Paris, France, who played a significant role in the Seven Years' War.

As a military leader, he commanded the French forces in North America, contributing to the defeat of the British at the Battle of Fort Duquesne in 1758.

His military victories led to the cession of the Ohio River Valley to France, securing its territorial claims in North America.

De Noailles's military successes had a lasting impact on the French-American relations and the territorial disputes between France and Britain in North America.

In his later years, de Noailles was known for his conservative views and his efforts to modernize the French military.

Quoting de Noailles, 'The true glory of war lies not in victory, but in the knowledge that we have fought for the cause of freedom.'
